# Parsed

Arguments that matched a command.

```rux
pub struct Parsed {
    // private fields
}
```

`Copy`, owning nothing: it borrows the specification and the arguments, both of which must outlive it.

<h3 id="count"><code>Count</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Count(self: &Parsed, name: char8[..]) -> uint
```

How many times the option with long name `name` was given.
Counting is how `-vvv` means more than `-v`. An option the command does not declare was given zero times.
Runs in time linear in the number of arguments and allocates nothing.

| Name   | Type        | Description                               |
| ------ | ----------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `name` | `char8[..]` | the option's long name without its dashes |

**Returns**: the number of times it was given

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/CommandLine/Src/Parsed.rux#L211)

<h3 id="value"><code>Value</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Value(
    self: &Parsed,
    name: char8[..]
) -> OsStringView?
```

The value of the option with long name `name`, the last one given when it was given more than once.
The last value wins so that a later argument can override an earlier one, as a script adding to a fixed command
line expects. Runs in time linear in the number of arguments and allocates nothing.

| Name   | Type        | Description                               |
| ------ | ----------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `name` | `char8[..]` | the option's long name without its dashes |

**Returns**: the value as typed, or none when the option was not given or takes no value

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/CommandLine/Src/Parsed.rux#L236)

<h3 id="integer"><code>Integer</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Integer(
    self: &Parsed,
    name: char8[..]
) -> int64? ! CommandLineError
```

The value of the option or positional named `name` read as a decimal integer, or none when it was not given.
An optional leading `-` or `+` is accepted, then one or more decimal digits and nothing else. Reports
`InvalidValue` for any other text and for a number outside the range of `int64`. Allocates nothing.

| Name   | Type        | Description                                   |
| ------ | ----------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `name` | `char8[..]` | an option's long name, or a positional's name |

**Returns**: the number, none when the value was not given, or why it is not a number

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/CommandLine/Src/Parsed.rux#L310)

## Related

<h3 id="parse"><code>Parse</code></h3>

```rux
pub func Parse(
    spec: *CommandSpec,
    arguments: OsStringView[..]
) -> Parsed ! CommandLineError
```

Checks `arguments` against `spec`.
`arguments` are the arguments after the program's name. Reports the first mismatch: an unknown option, an option
missing its value or given one it does not take, an unknown or missing subcommand, a missing required positional,
or an argument beyond what the command accepts. Asking for `--help` or `--version` succeeds whatever else is
missing, and [`HelpRequested`](/docs/api/commandline/parsed#help-requested) or [`VersionRequested`](/docs/api/commandline/parsed#version-requested) then says so. Allocates nothing; both `spec` and `arguments`
must outlive the result.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/CommandLine/Src/Parsed.rux#L91)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type               | Description                               |
| ----------- | ------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `spec`      | `*CommandSpec`     | the command the arguments are for         |
| `arguments` | `OsStringView[..]` | the arguments, without the program's name |

**Returns**: the parse, or why the arguments do not match

<h3 id="parse-process"><code>ParseProcess</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ParseProcess(spec: *CommandSpec) -> Parsed ! CommandLineError
```

Checks the process's own arguments against `spec`.
The same checks as [`Parse`](/docs/api/commandline/parsed#parse), over every argument after the program's name. The arguments last as long as the
process; `spec` must outlive the result.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/CommandLine/Src/Parsed.rux#L101)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type           | Description                       |
| ------ | -------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `spec` | `*CommandSpec` | the command the arguments are for |

**Returns**: the parse, or why the arguments do not match

<h3 id="argument-source"><code>ArgumentSource</code></h3>

```rux
pub variant ArgumentSource {
    Given(OsStringView[..]),
    ProcessArguments
}
```

Where the arguments being parsed come from.
`Copy`. A slice is borrowed and must outlive every parse made from it; the process's own arguments last as long as
the process.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/CommandLine/Src/Scan.rux#L18)

**Cases**

| Name                      | Description                                           |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `Given(OsStringView[..])` | Arguments given as views, without the program's name. |
| `ProcessArguments`        | The process's own arguments after the program's name. |
